grh_91f8950a1d03b2ac4ec8.title: Then There Were None
paragraphs: The crew of the spaceship Omega lands on a seemingly alien world after finding signs of a civilization that does not appear on their charts. Explorers are killed by enormous spider-like and reptilian creatures, violent 'earthquakes' and sudden torrents of water, leaving Commander Austin Baker and two women to abandon the ship and search for shelter. They encounter gigantic ants and discover an immense sneaker, suggesting the planet's inhabitants are colossal. The final scene shifts perspective to an ordinary suburban backyard: the mysterious floods are lawn sprinklers, the sneaker belongs to a child, and the tiny spacecraft is mistaken for one of his toys, revealing that the explorers have been struggling through a familiar world at miniature scale.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on February 23, 1979. It is listed as episode 15 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Keith Andes, Peter Leeds, Sam Edwards, Janet Waldo, and Mary Jane Croft. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Ted Sherdeman as writer, and Richard Widmark as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_916991b434ed44d770c4.title: The Last Land Rush
paragraphs: In an overcrowded future, the government opens highway divider land to private homesteading, triggering a deadly modern land rush. A young couple crosses the highway, stakes a claim and spends the night defending it from other desperate people, including a mother with a sick baby who also wants a place of her own. By the noon deadline the couple manages to remain on the claim and is declared among the new landowners. Their victory feels hollow after the violence, fear and selfishness required to secure a tiny patch of ground in a society that has run out of room.
